Passives in four registers

Source: R/data.R
passives.Rd

Number of passive constructions in 400 texts, 100 each from conversation, fiction, news and academic writing. Texts differ in length, so counts need an exposure term. The counts are overdispersed.

Usage

passives

Format

A tibble with 400 rows and 4 columns:

text

Text ID, T001 to T400.

register

"conversation", "fiction", "news" or "academic".

words

Text length in words.

passives

Number of passives.

Source

data-raw/passives.R

Details

True model: negative binomial with mean rate * words / 1000 and size 4, where rate per 1000 words is 2 (conversation), 5 (fiction), 10 (news) and 20 (academic). Biber, Conrad and Leech (2002) note that passive verbs are about ten times more frequent in academic prose than in conversation. The other rates and all data are simulated.

References

Biber, D., Conrad, S. & Leech, G. (2002). Longman Student Grammar of Spoken and Written English. Harlow: Longman.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- MASS::glm.nb(passives ~ 0 + register + offset(log(words / 1000)), data = passives)
  exp(coef(m))
  m$theta
}
